name: Dark Forest Green
lede: Dark Forest Green is a near-black green from the 2010 xkcd color survey, a darker sibling of Forest Green that four separate 1955 ISCC-NBS names also crowd around within a few units.

sections.title: One shade, five names
sections.body: The xkcd survey records this as *dark* plus the existing name [[forest-green]], while its sibling Light Forest Green adds the opposite modifier to the same base [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system independently crowds four of its own names into the same small patch of color space: Dark Bottle Green, Dark Hunter Green, Elephant Green and Winter, all cataloguing shades close enough to be called the same color [2]. The color library finds the closest ISCC-NBS block, very dark yellowish green, only 2.2 units away, a tight match [2]. In Munsell terms it sits at 8.1GY 1.4/5.0, and in LCH at lightness 15, chroma 32, hue 142 degrees, among the darkest, most saturated greens in the library [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our 23,781-painting archive, a color within six units of Dark Forest Green covers at least one per cent of the canvas in 13 paintings, about 0.05 percent of the archive, as photographed, rarer than 77 percent of the named colors tracked [3]. Its earliest match, Jean Hey's panel dated 1490, is 520 years before the xkcd name itself was recorded in 2010; that gap only shows a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, since near-black greens like this are common in old varnished shadows regardless of what anyone called them, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. In printed English the phrase rose fastest in the 1990s and peaked in the 2010s, tracking the rise of web color names generally [4].
